title: A million vs. a billion seconds
concept: Counting one number per second: 1,000,000 takes about 11.6 days, 1,000,000,000 takes about 31.7 years (1,000 times longer).
kept: Question: how long to count to a million and a billion at one number per second
Student's facts (about 11 days, about 31 years) which are correct
Misconception that a billion is just a bit more than a million
Timelines compared to a life, both shown
Guess first, then show both timelines
filled_in: Guess is multiple choice about the billion
Evidence is a count-ahead set of buttons (1 day, 1 year, 10 years) that fills both bars
Life length set to 80 years, with an age slider to place the timelines
Stepped notes after reaching a million and a billion

changed.what: Student's 'like 11 days' is shown as 11 days 14 hours (11.6 days)
changed.why: 1,000,000 / 86,400 = 11.57 days; the rounded figure was fine, the page shows the computed value
1e9 / (365.25 x 86,400) = 31.69; the design's 31 was rounded down

math_check: 1e6/86400=11.574 days (11 d + 49,600 s = 13.8 h); 1e9/86400=11,574 days; /365.25=31.69 years; all values computed in code from 86,400 s/day and 365.25 days/year. Checker passed with no problems or warnings; screenshots reviewed.
